scope: Four original worked cases and eight fully solved advanced exercises, fixed-policy minimum proof, exact funded journal and collateral inventory, ALM value/income counterexample, dated entity/currency transfer case, answered teach-back and delayed retention. Synthetic finite assumptions and historical method context; no current regulatory ratio, legal entitlement, stress probability or universal funding optimum.

proof_audit.audit: Defines usable initial cash, scenario/date-specific receipts and obligations, exact eligible receipt-before-payment order, no missing intermediate deadline or payment-dependent receipt, and a timely independent nonmaturing cash contribution without interest/cost/policy response. Induction proves H(b)=H(0)+b. A negative prefix proves necessity; nonnegative prefixes plus receipt order prove every intermediate payment can be paid. Finite maximum, equality and zero requirement are handled. Explicit limitations cover currency/entity restrictions, changed policy, late contributions and maturing bridges. No probability or least-cost conclusion.

Old principal and already-accrued interest stay payable when new rollover disappears. New term and secured loans have exact draws, principal maturities and three interval-interest accruals. Secured interest for the first interval uses principal before the cutoff-2 paydown. All principal and margin transfers preserve equity; stipulated cash variation changes equity; accrued new interest changes equity/payable before payment. Customer advance becomes a loan. Full-payment diagnostic rows after a failed cash prefix are expressly hypothetical and may show negative total cash; no overdraft or default mechanism is silently invented.

Advance per unit (1-h)p is positive on the declared domain. Remaining principal=min(draw,eligible pool capacity), paydown=max(0,draw-capacity), and pledged units=remaining principal/advance prove nonnegative free inventory and the exact pool identity. Old encumbrance and inaccessible custody units are excluded. Principal-only coverage and separately payable interest are stipulated; no universal repo convention is claimed. Maturity releases new collateral after repayment, with no reuse to fund it.

Finite discounted cash sums are differentiated termwise. Floating par follows a telescoping coupon identity including zero yield without dividing by yield; the lab supports negative flat yields greater than -1 within its bounded interval. Coupled coupon resetting and flat valuation rate, no credit spread/floor/default, unremunerated cash and fixed principal maturity are explicit. Positive EVE sensitivity and negative one-year NII sensitivity follow from separate horizon/contract effects, with correct percentage-point/basis-point units and exact-versus-local distinction.

Keeping all other policy cash fixed, initial borrowing adds b to cutoffs1-3 while maturity repayment leaves terminal effect -gb. Early bound39.9 and terminal bound3.81/g imply exact [39.9,190.5] at g=.02 and incompatibility with38.1 at g=.10. This is conditional feasibility, not an optimal financing recommendation.

remaining_limits: All scenarios and contract rates are synthetic; there is no empirical validation or probability calibration.
Four-cutoff receipt ordering, collateral delivery, counterparty performance and legally available transfers are stipulated assumptions. Additional timing or legal constraints require a finer plan.
The book carrying amounts and marked-equity proxy do not implement full accounting rules, loan credit valuation or a regulatory capital/liquidity definition.

The cash minimum is conditional on a fixed policy and nonmaturing cash reserve. No minimum-cost optimization, automatic official support, endogenous run, sale feedback, default waterfall or infinite-horizon survival theorem is claimed.
Separate peer/coordinator acceptance and shared build/offline/UI/publication gates remain pending and are root-owned.
